title: Rawframe BaselineRecord, generation 1
description: The fourth and last authority of the ADR-0019 chain, per SPEC-0014. It is a reviewed promotion pointer to one passing Evaluation Receipt, authored by a human review action and never emitted by a tool. This generation has a schema and a reader and no writer: the generation that admits a writer is a later generation with a trusted builder behind it. Because the shared trust definition pins provenance to diagnostic_untrusted, no record this schema admits can be a real promotion, which is the intended ceiling rather than a limitation to be worked around.

role.description: SPEC-0014's two roles and nothing else. A role is fixed at authoring; a record whose role changed is a different record with a successor pointing at it.

tier.description: Tier 0 is the only tier this gate can produce, so it is the only tier a record here can name. Canonical Tier-2 evidence requires a qualified cell that does not exist yet, and admitting the value it would carry would be a future flag with nothing behind it.

compatibility.description: SPEC-0014's exact compatibility key. Every dimension must match exactly for a comparison to mean anything, so each is named here rather than summarized into one opaque hash that hides which dimension moved.

cellFingerprint.description: The ADR-0020 benchmark cell this evidence came from. A local developer machine is not a cell, which is one more reason a record at this tier cannot be promoted.

promoted.description: What is being pointed at, by descriptor rather than by path or name. A human-readable name may resolve to an immutable digest but is never the authority.

aggregateVerdict.description: Fixed. SPEC-0014 admits promotion only of a passing aggregate verdict, so a record naming any other value is not a weaker promotion, it is not a promotion.

source.description: The candidate's own identity. Kept separate from the review identity below so that a promotion arriving inside the change it approves is visible rather than implied.

predecessor.description: The chain, stated one way or the other and never left to inference. Exactly one of an explicit first-baseline marker and a predecessor descriptor is present, so a broken chain is a refusal rather than a record that reads as a beginning.

chain.description: Earlier records in role order, newest first. Bounded because a chain nobody can read is a chain nobody checks.

promotion.description: The reviewed human act. Every member here is authored, which is why this tool validates the record and never produces one: it carries a clock and a named person, and a deterministic emitter can honestly supply neither.

approvalAuthority.description: Fixed. SPEC-0016 reserves this act to the project owner, and an enum with a second member would be the beginning of an agent-approvable path.

approvalTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC, seconds resolution, Z only. Offsets and fractional seconds are refused because two spellings of one instant are two byte sequences for one record.

affected.description: What this baseline is a reference for. A promotion that names no metric is a promotion of nothing and is refused rather than treated as covering everything.

headroom.description: How much room is left against what this record is a reference for. Absolute headroom is against a ceiling or objective; relative headroom is against another baseline and is unavailable before ADR-0020 cell qualification, which is why an entry of that kind at this tier is refused rather than reported as zero.

retention.description: When this record is reviewed again and when its required attachments stop being kept. SPEC-0014 requires that ending retention deliberately produce a successor authority rather than an active baseline whose evidence has quietly gone.

status.description: The status relationship, not a mutable field. A record never stops being active by being edited; a later immutable record supersedes or revokes it, and this record names that successor once it exists.

claimScope.description: What validating this record does not mean. Every member is fixed false by the schema rather than by convention, for the same reason the EvaluationReceipt carries one: a promotion record is exactly the artifact that gets quoted out of context, and it has to argue against that reading in its own bytes.

scaledValue.description: SPEC-0017's fixed-point subset, the same pair the EvaluationReceipt uses. A fractional margin is carried exactly by an integer pair and never by a float.
